title: on SQLite the claim's mutual exclusion is the immediate transaction, and the claim carries no locking clause because there is nothing left for one to do
scope:
what arbitrates a claim on the one backend with a single writer, and where the primitive
that provides it sits. It does not touch the claim's shape on the other dialects, which is
[0084](0084.md)'s, and it decides nothing about how many workers an operator runs.

summary.headline: On SQLite a queue claim is an immediate transaction, and that is the lock
summary.body:
SQLite has a single writer, so inside an immediate transaction no other connection is writing
and two workers cannot claim the same job; the row-locking clause the other databases use would
do nothing there and is not written. The transaction is opened as immediate rather than deferred
because a read followed by a write would otherwise try to upgrade a shared lock, which SQLite
refuses without waiting. Nothing about this is visible from a program.
